supportsExplain.description: Indicates whether the SQL engine supports the EXPLAIN statement.

useUnquotedColumns.description:
If true, column names will be used without quoted identifiers in generated SQL.
For example: SELECT id FROM table instead of SELECT "id" FROM table.
WARNING: Columns which contain special characters will not be escaped and will cause malformed queries!

useUnquotedTables.description: If true, table names will be used without quoted identifiers in generated SQL.

requiresLimitBeforeOffset.description:
Indicates whether the SQL dialect requires the LIMIT clause to appear
before the OFFSET clause. Some databases enforce this ordering.

requiresLimitIfOffset.description:
Indicates whether the OFFSET clause must be accompanied by a LIMIT clause.
If true, OFFSET cannot be used alone.

openingEscapeCharacter.description:
The beginning escape character used for quoting SQL identifiers.
By default, this is double quotes.

closingEscapeCharacter.description:
The ending escape character used for quoting SQL identifiers.
By default, this is double quotes.

reservedColumns.description: Special columns or "pseudocolumns" which should never be quoted in SQL

supportsFullyQualifiedTables.description:
Indicates whether the SQL engine supports using fully qualified table names.
For example: SELECT id FROM <schema>.<tableName>

defaultTimestampFormat.description: The default timestamp format used for SQL queries.

disableOrderingById.description:
When performing a fetch on entity types, C3 Agentic AI Platform will query the database with default ordering using
the entity id to ensure reliable paging. Since, it is not always possible to order by id in SQL due to several
factors such as lack of indexes, non-performant database engines, etc. in external data stores that lead to
performance issues, this option allows to disable the default ordering behavior.

title: Defines SQL-level capabilities and behaviors specific to a given SQL engine.
name: SqlEngine.SqlInfo
